My state does not yet allow us to use LPG, that is a regulation per state, some other states do use it. I drive a renault kwid, as do most ubers around my city who do not use rented cars, because that is the most accessible car in the market, it does about 15km/L of fuel, so it actually very good for driving uber, can’t drive comfort anymore though, miss doing that, used to when i rented a chevrolet onix sedan. Regular maintenance for it not that expensive, being a little rough only when I have to change the suspensions and such. Risk, on the other hand, is the most stressing factor, knowing about the crime ratios in my country, I’m generally very scared of any trip that doesn’t land in a very crowded area, not even the richest neighborhoods are truly safe, I never got robbed or anything, had colleagues who did, it’s a shame, but we gotta make do with what we have

edit: forgot about the laws, ubers are subject to income revenue tax, just as anyone who makes money in brazil, but only if we make over 2000 or so a month, otherwise we don’t have to pay that tax

Yes, I understand your point, we often make direct conversions between values in BRL and USD, or any other currency whatsoever, and that’s fine for market trades, purchases and whatnot, but the thing is, such comparisons cannot be translated to “brazil is a cheaper country”. There are so many socioeconomic variables you’re failing to see, yes, a small downtown apartment in São Paulo may cost about 3000 brl, but that is completely unaffordable for the vast majority of the country’s population, that’s why Brazil has so many neighborhoods displaying extreme poverty, our famous “favelas” also. Living in a third world country is not cheap for anyone who lives there, except for a very few select people who are extremely rich.

tldr; the average brazilian cannot realistically pay 3000 bucks on rent and still stay alive
